literal: Having made protection, not yielding, of mean people, the worthless friendship, than obtaining, not obtaining is good.
translation: Rather than acquiring the worthless friendship of mean people, which does not yield any protection even when cultivated, it is far better not to acquire it at all.
modern: பாதுகாப்பைத் தராத கீழ் குணமுடையவர்களின் தீய நட்பைப் பெறுவதை விட, அதனைப் பெறாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the futility of forming alliances with base or mean-minded individuals. The poet describes their relationship as 'புன்கேண்மை' (worthless friendship) because, even if one puts effort into cultivating it, it fails to provide any safety or support ('ஏமம் சாரா') when needed. Therefore, the couplet concludes that not acquiring ('எய்தாமை') such a friendship is far better ('நன்று') than acquiring ('எய்தலின்') it, as it only brings vulnerability instead of security.
